old_description: under the same owner for since 2006. Our experts manage all aspects of your residential or commercial solar installation project in St. Louis, MO, from design to build, and our full-time Service team is here to care for your system for decades.
about:
StraightUp Solar is a solar installation company based in St. Louis, Missouri, founded in 2006 and operating under the same ownership since its inception. The company was established to empower St. Louis area residents and businesses to take control of their energy with clean solar options.

The firm provides end-to-end solar photovoltaic services, including system design, installation, battery storage integration, EV charger installation, and ongoing operations and maintenance. Its full-time, in-house service department handles monitoring, troubleshooting, remove-and-reinstall work, and commissioning for both residential and commercial arrays. Since 2006, the team has completed more than 3,200 solar installations across eastern Missouri and central and southern Illinois.

StraightUp Solar serves homeowners as well as a diverse commercial client base that includes small businesses, nonprofits, schools, agricultural operations, government facilities, industrial sites, and houses of worship. The company manages grid-tied distributed generation projects that offset utility electricity use and provides monitoring portals for real-time production tracking.

The company emphasizes its continuity of ownership and a dedicated service department as key differentiators, aiming to remain a long-term solar partner for customers through design, build, and decades of system care.

about:
Sumiden Wire Products Corporation was founded in 1979 in Stockton, California, as the first U.S. production facility established by Japan’s Sumitomo Electric Industries (SEI). The company operates as a wholly-owned subsidiary of SEI and is headquartered in Dickson, Tennessee.

The company manufactures seven-wire prestressed concrete steel strand (PC strand) to ASTM A416 specifications in uncoated, epoxy-coated, and stainless steel grades, as well as stainless spring wire, stainless medical wire, nickel-plated carbon steel wire, and industrial alloy products. Production spans three plants in California, Tennessee, and Texas, with capabilities including wire drawing, nickel electroplating to custom thicknesses, epoxy coating, and dedicated inventory programs for medical customers. Environmental Product Declarations are available for each PC strand variant.

Sumiden Wire serves the construction industry — supplying strand for bridges, buildings, parking structures, and home foundations — along with aerospace, automotive, consumer, military, and medical device manufacturers. Medical applications include orthodontic wire, guidewires, orthopaedic components, and endoscopy devices. The company also supports durable goods producers.

Sumiden Wire states its mission is to “help Build America” by providing superior-quality steel strand for concrete structures nationwide. Differentiators cited include its global supplier network, seasoned local management, customer service, and innovations such as stainless steel and epoxy-coated PC strand plus ultra-fine wire for surgical catheters. As part of the Sumitomo Electric Group, the company adheres to the group’s Code of Conduct.

Sumitomo Electric Wiring Systems (SEWS) was established in 1987 as the North American arm of Japan’s Sumitomo Group, a conglomerate with a 400-year heritage. The company operates its North American headquarters from Farmington Hills, Michigan, and maintains additional locations across the continent under the leadership of President Kazuyoshi Nakai.

SEWS designs, develops, and manufactures wiring harnesses, electronic components, electric wire, and electrified-vehicle-related products for the automotive sector. Its portfolio spans complete harness assemblies, integrated electronics, and advanced product development services aimed at systems integration and modularization. The company emphasizes advanced manufacturing technology and global technical development across its North American footprint.

The company serves automotive original equipment manufacturers and tier suppliers, providing electrical distribution systems that address safety, comfort, fuel economy, and connectivity requirements. Its products are engineered for the evolving “automotive society” that connects vehicles, people, and infrastructure.

SEWS states its mission is to be the global leader delivering innovative electrical distribution systems that meet the demands of the ever-changing automotive market. name: Sumner Woodworker Store
old_description: specializes in drum and brush sanders for the woodworking and metalworking industries. From our exceptional product quality to our customer service and technical support, we have the experience and application expertise to assist you in your sanding and finishing needs. We are located in St. Paul, Minnesota.
about:
Sumner Woodworker Store operates in Sumner, Washington, in a building with roots dating back to 1889. The business has been family-owned since 1996, when John and Joan Schmit — John a former Boeing executive who restored classic wooden boats — decided to open a woodworking store in a property they were renovating. The Schmit family's personal passion for woodcraft shaped the store's founding mission.

The store runs a nearly 10,000-square-foot retail facility stocked with woodworking tools, supplies, and a wide selection of exotic and premium woods. It carries brands such as SuperMax drum sanders, SawStop professional cabinet saws, Robert Sorby woodturning tools, and Colwood wood-burning tools. Every tool sold is inspected, assembled, and tested before it leaves the store. The inventory includes nearly 100 species of wood, plus turning blocks, carving blocks, and pen-making materials. The staff is composed entirely of experienced woodworkers who provide hands-on product guidance.

The store serves hobbyist and professional woodworkers, woodcarvers, and some metalworkers. Its customer base ranges from DIY enthusiasts and small-shop professionals to woodturners seeking specialized tools and materials. It positions itself as a one-stop shop for woodworking and wood carving in Washington state.

The Schmit family started the business to offer a knowledgeable, non-commercialized alternative to big-box retailers. They differentiate by ensuring tools are ready to run out the door, maintaining deep product expertise, and preserving a historical store environment that reflects the community's woodworking heritage.

Sun Comm Technologies, Inc. was founded in 1993 in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and has since provided television programming and high-speed internet services to residential and commercial customers across New Mexico, West Texas, eastern Arizona, and southern Colorado. The privately held company began as a satellite TV provider and expanded into a multi-carrier authorized retailer.

The company acts as an authorized retailer and installer for major satellite and internet brands including DISH, DIRECTV, Spectrum, CenturyLink, HughesNet, and Viasat. It designs and installs integrated cable systems for hospitality, healthcare, and institutional clients, deploying 10 to 75 receivers per property. Services span satellite TV installation, broadband provisioning, and in-room entertainment casting solutions for hotels.

Sun Comm serves a diverse client base: hotels and motels, hospitals and assisted-living facilities, correctional institutions, military bases, state and federal government offices, college dormitories, and bars and restaurants. Residential customers in Albuquerque, Santa Fe, Las Cruces, and El Paso also make up a significant portion of its business.

The company emphasizes a single-point-of-contact model, guiding customers through multi-provider options to match programming and bandwidth needs. Its website highlights bilingual support and rapid deployment, with typical installation quoted at one to two days.

about:
Sun Medical Equipment & Supplies was founded in 1979 in Troy, Michigan, as a locally owned and operated business serving the home health needs of patients across Oakland, Macomb, and Wayne Counties. The company began with a focus on providing durable medical equipment and in-home care services that allow customers to remain comfortable at home.

The company operates a retail store in Troy and an online catalog, supplying home medical equipment from brands such as Philips, LIFEPAK, and AirMini. Its product range includes CPAP machines, AEDs, cold therapy systems, mobility aids, hospital beds, oxygen and respiratory equipment, bath safety items, compression garments, orthotic braces, wound care supplies, and power scooters. Sun Medical also provides in-home care staffed by nurses, home health aides, and caregivers, overseen by a registered nurse. The staff offers expertise in mobility equipment fitting, orthotic and compression garment fitting, Medicare billing, and home modification installation.

Sun Medical serves individual patients, union members (who receive exclusive discounts), and healthcare providers such as Corewell Health. The company works with professional organizations including the National Homecare & Hospice Association, the Michigan Homecare & Hospice Association, the Michigan Spinal Cord Injury Association, and the Case Management Society of America.

The company emphasizes its accreditation by the Community Health Accreditation Partner, Inc., and its commitment to staying at the forefront of industry changes to deliver quality service. old_description: Discover the true cost of solar energy. Voted the #1 Residential Solar Installer in Missouri. Discover the true cost of solar energy. Voted the #1 Residential Solar Installer in Missouri. Learn about the upfront expenses, long-term savings, and government incentives for solar.
about:
Sun Solar LLC was founded in 2012 by Caleb Arthur in Houston, Missouri, before moving its headquarters to Springfield, Missouri. Arthur, a former law enforcement officer, turned to solar after a career-ending injury, initially installing a ground-mount system on his own property and then selling and installing systems door-to-door. The company now serves Missouri, Kansas, and Illinois from its Springfield base.

The company provides turnkey solar installation services for residential and commercial customers, handling design, permitting, coordination, installation, electrification, and ongoing service. Its offerings include rooftop and ground-mount solar arrays, Tesla Solar Roof installations (the first in Missouri), and Tesla Powerwall battery backup systems. A dedicated Smart Energy Solutions division adds energy-efficiency upgrades such as LED lighting, attic sealing, and insulation. Financing options span loans, cash purchases, and power purchase agreements.

Sun Solar works primarily with homeowners and businesses across the three-state region. Residential clients include individual households seeking energy independence, while commercial customers range from small businesses to larger facilities such as the Denton Embassy Suites. The company also partners with Everbright Exteriors for roofing services.

Arthur’s “reduce before you produce” philosophy drives the firm’s focus on energy efficiency alongside solar generation, aiming to lower both utility bills and environmental impact. The company emphasizes in-house installation crews and a single-point-of-contact model to streamline the customer experience.

old_description: SunCommon has been operating in Vermont since 2012 and in New York since 2002! As the most tenured local solar company in our regions, we’re deeply committed to these beautiful communities. We’re dedicated to this place just like you, which means we’re equally invested in creating stronger, more vibrant communities together for years to come.
about:
SunCommon is headquartered in Waterbury, Vermont, and has been operating in New York since 2002 and in Vermont since 2012. The company was founded in 2002 and is structured as a certified B Corporation and a benefit corporation, reflecting a mission-driven ownership model that balances profit with social and environmental impact.

The company provides full-service solar and energy storage installation for residential, commercial, agricultural, non-profit, and municipal customers. Its services cover roof-mounted and ground-mounted solar arrays, battery backup systems (including Tesla Powerwall), electric vehicle charger installation, and community solar array development. SunCommon manages the entire project lifecycle — planning, financing, permitting, design, engineering, and construction — and reports having served over 10,000 customers across its two-state territory.

SunCommon’s customer base spans homeowners, businesses, farms, non-profits, and municipalities in Vermont and New York. Specific examples include residential rooftop and ground-mount systems, commercial solar projects that qualify for additional incentives, farm installations described as a “no-brainer” by the company, and community solar arrays that allow multiple utility customers to share the output of a single one-acre array through group net metering.

The company says its distinguishing features are its status as the most tenured local solar provider in its regions, its certification as a B Corporation and benefit corporation, and its mission to accelerate the transition to solar power because “ensuring a habitable planet is the most important work of our lifetimes.” It also notes being named the reader’s choice for solar and batteries since 2016.

about:
Sunbelt Packaging LLC began in 1980 in York, South Carolina, as a supplier of specialty products for niche applications in the textile industry. The company expanded into flexible packaging materials to leverage its service reputation and grew through acquisitions into a global provider. Today it operates as part of BradyPLUS Company, a larger platform offering tailored solutions for janitorial/sanitation, foodservice, and industrial packaging markets.

The firm supplies a range of flexible packaging materials including flexible intermediate bulk containers (FIBC), stretch films, shrink wrap, and strapping. It also sells and supports automated packaging equipment such as stretch wrappers, automatic strapping machines, palletizing robots with payloads from 6 kg to 1,200 kg, and continuous-motion wraparound case packers. Sunbelt services customers across all 50 U.S. states, Canada, Mexico, South America, and Singapore.

Its customer base spans manufacturing and distribution operations, with specific focus on the JanSan, foodservice, and industrial packaging sectors. The company’s heritage in textiles informs its approach to niche applications, while its current portfolio addresses broad packaging needs for industrial and consumer goods producers.

Sunbelt emphasizes its broad product offering, deep technical knowledge, and unique sourcing capabilities as the foundation of a customer-service-first culture. The leadership frames continuous improvement and reinvestment as the path to secure long-term partnerships, positioning the company as a supplier that aligns with growth-oriented customers.
